sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house in North Bergen, NJ?
sections.html:
North Bergen sellers can list the house, sell it privately or accept an as-is cash purchase, and the right choice depends on whether the house has tenants, a hillside lot or open code issues. North Bergen is a township of 5.14 square miles of land that the Census Bureau estimates at 61,483 residents, a drop of 3.0% from its 2020 base. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 41.6% and the typical owner-occupied home value at $473,500.

Before choosing, collect the paperwork a buyer or title company will ask for.

  • The deed and your most recent tax bill.
  • Any Certificate of Occupancy for the building and its legal unit count.
  • Rent control registration, if any unit is rented.
  • Lease copies and rent ledgers for each tenant.

sections.h2: What is the land like in North Bergen?
sections.html:
North Bergen is shaped like an inverted L, with a long east to west northern section and a north to south section between Secaucus and the Hudson-facing towns of Guttenberg, West New York and Union City. The Hudson River forms the eastern border, facing Manhattan, and the township touches Carlstadt across the Hackensack River. The Palisades rise from the waterfront, and a slope on the west side drops toward the Meadowlands.

The slope on the west side makes North Bergen the city with the second most hills per square mile in the United States, after San Francisco. For a seller, steep driveways, retaining walls and stairs up to the front door are features a buyer will want to inspect, so photograph and describe them honestly.

Low-lying ground on the west side is part of the New Jersey Meadowlands, so ask your insurance agent whether your parcel sits in a flood zone before you quote a closing date.

sections.h2: Which North Bergen neighborhoods should I name in a listing?
sections.html:
Name the section, because North Bergen's neighborhoods differ in housing type and in access to transit.

  • Bergenline Avenue, a long commercial avenue with more than 300 retail stores and restaurants.
  • The Racetrack section, on the plateau between Bergenline Avenue and Kennedy Boulevard.
  • Bergenwood, on the steep slopes of the west side of the Palisades.
  • New Durham, near the Bergen Turnpike and Tonnelle Avenue.
  • Meadowview, behind the Municipal Building, and Babbitt in the Meadowlands district.
  • Bulls Ferry and Woodcliff, on the Hudson side near North Hudson Park.

The area was inhabited by the Hackensack band of the Lenape before Dutch repurchase in 1658, and the township was incorporated on April 10, 1843. Many Spanish speakers arrived beginning in the 1960s, earning the nickname Havana on the Hudson. The Census Bureau shows that 71.4% of residents are Hispanic or Latino and 74.5% speak a language other than English at home, so listings in Spanish reach a large share of local buyers.

sections.h2: How do transit and schools affect North Bergen sales?
sections.html:
Commuters buy here for the buses and light rail. Route 495 runs between the Lincoln Tunnel and the New Jersey Turnpike, and NJ Transit lines 121, 125, 127 and 128 among others end at the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown. Jitneys on Bergenline Avenue run as often as one bus a minute. The Hudson-Bergen Light Rail stops at Tonnelle Avenue and connects to Weehawken, Hoboken, Jersey City and Bayonne.

The Census Bureau reports a mean commute of 33.1 minutes, so a block near a bus line or a light rail stop is worth highlighting. The North Bergen School District serves pre-kindergarten through grade 12 and, in 2023-24, enrolled 7,165 students across eight schools.

sections.h2: What local rules apply to a North Bergen two family or rental?
sections.html:
North Bergen has its own rent control ordinance, run by the township's Rent Control office, which explains which apartments are covered and what the legal base rent is. The office keeps files on residential properties for public inspection. The township's FAQ gives an annual increase of 2.5 percent of base rent, allowed once within a twelve month period, with at least 30 days' notice to tenants after approval.

Renovations to occupied or vacant units must be processed through the Rent Control office, with inspections before and after. A landlord who plans to rent to a Section 8 tenant files a Certificate of Exemption, and the township lists a fee of $100 for it. Check with the office whether your building is covered before you give a buyer a rent roll.

Short-term rentals are tightly restricted. Ordinance 610-23, adopted September 20, 2023, bars short-term rentals by anyone who had not registered a dwelling as of September 6, 2023, so do not market a house to buyers on the strength of Airbnb income unless the property already holds a registration certificate.

sections.h2: What does the Code Enforcement office require before a sale?
sections.html:
North Bergen's Code Enforcement office inspects and issues residential and commercial certificates of occupancy and investigates illegal occupancy. Its number is 201-392-2051. The township website also lists a Residential Owner Certificate form and an illegal apartment hotline, so ask the office which certificate applies to your sale and whether any unit count in your deed differs from what exists.

If your mortgage is in default, note that Ordinance 325-17 requires the mortgagee to inspect and register the property with the Building Department within 10 days, stating whether it is vacant or occupied. Owners facing default can ask the Building Department how that registration works.

sections.h2: What fees and forms come with a North Bergen closing?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state Realty Transfer Fee, and for a median North Bergen price of $473,500 the over-$350,000 schedule applies, topping out at $4.80 per $500 between $200,000 and $550,000. The fee does not apply to a deed from an executor or administrator to an heir or devisee under a will or the intestacy laws, which matters for inherited houses. A deed recorded within 90 days of a divorce decree is also exempt.

On prices above $1,000,000 the state adds a graduated percent fee, 1% up to $2,000,000 and more above that. A nonresident heir or seller prepays gross income tax of at least 2% of consideration, and the estimate is 10.75% of the gain if that is higher.

Hudson County deeds are recorded by the Hudson County Register of Deeds and Mortgages at 257 Cornelison Avenue, second floor, Jersey City. The cashier's window and search area are open weekdays from 9:00 am to 2:00 pm, and customer service answers phones from 8:00 am to 3:45 pm at 201-395-4760. The Register also offers a free Recording Notification Service to warn owners of fraud.

faqs.q: Can I sell a North Bergen house that has an illegal apartment?
faqs.a: A sale can go ahead, but tell buyers up front. The township's Code Enforcement office investigates illegal occupancy and runs an illegal apartment hotline, so call 201-392-2051 and ask what a buyer or lender will need before closing.

faqs.q: Does North Bergen have rent control?
faqs.a: Yes. The township's Rent Control office administers the ordinance, and its FAQ lists an annual increase of 2.5 percent of base rent, once in twelve months, with at least 30 days' notice to tenants. Registration is required for covered rentals.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run my North Bergen house as an Airbnb?
faqs.a: Generally no. Ordinance 610-23 ended new short-term rental registrations after September 6, 2023, and only dwellings that held a registration certificate by then are grandfathered. Confirm with the township before advertising it that way.

faqs.q: Do I pay the transfer fee if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Not on the executor's deed that moves the house to an heir under the will or intestacy law. If you then sell the house to a buyer, you are the seller and the fee applies to that second deed.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a North Bergen sale?
faqs.a: At the Hudson County Register of Deeds and Mortgages, 257 Cornelison Avenue, second floor, in Jersey City. Your title company or attorney normally submits it with the realty transfer fee affidavit and the seller's residency form.
